questions.explanation: The form "aprirebbero" is the conditional form for "loro" of "aprire". Identifying the infinitive behind a conjugated form requires matching the stem and the person endings to the correct conjugation pattern.
questions.hint: Strip the ending and match the remaining stem to an infinitive.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: A review lesson presents one ending as practice. Which definite article precedes "occhi"?

options.misconception: reserved for z or s-plus-consonant words

questions.explanation: "occhi" is the plural of "occhio". It is masculine plural and begins with a vowel, so the article is "gli". Article form depends on gender, number, and the initial sound.
questions.hint: Decide the gender and number of the plural noun, then check its first letter.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: In a conjugation practice, the instructor notes a key term before answering. Choose the subjunctive: "loro cucinare".

options.misconception: this is the noi form of the verb, not loro
this is the voi form of the verb, not loro
this is the io form of the verb, not loro

questions.explanation: The subjunctive form of "cucinare" for "loro" is "cucinino". The present subjunctive is used after expressions of doubt, wish, or necessity. It draws its stem from the third-person plural present. Selecting the wrong person ending changes who performs the action.
questions.hint: Identify the subject pronoun, then apply the subjunctive ending for that person.

questions.subject: ITALIAN
questions.stem: Which indefinite article precedes "orologio"?
questions.explanation: The noun "orologio" is masculine and begins with a vowel, so the indefinite article is "un". Italian changes the indefinite article for gender and for vowel-initial words.
questions.hint: Match the article to both the gender and the first sound of the noun.
